newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CTBC to increase investment.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CTBC to increase investment.

text.p: Brazil's private telecom operator CTBC Telecom, onwed by Algar group, said it would increase its investments to 156 million reais in 1997 to improve its line and cellular telephone systems.
CTBC said in a statement it will invest 89 million reais to improve conventional telephone lines and 47.5 million reais in cellular telephone services.
The remainder will be invested in digitizing switching stations and installing optical cables to expand its data transmission lines to 1,800 kilometers, it said.
CTBC also plans to increase telephone lines to 360,000 this year from the current 330,000 and increase cellular telephone services by 70 percent to 110,000 users, it added.
The company said it was raising investments to prepare itself for growing competition after the privatization of Brazil's telecommunications sector.
CTBC Telecom is Brazil's sole telecom operator and is not part of the federal Telebras system.

It operates in 300 municipalities located in Brazil's center-south region, which includes Minas Gerais state industrial area, south of Goias state, north of Sao Paulo state and Mato Grosso do Sul state, the statement said. ((-- Romina Nicaretta, Sao Paulo Newsroom, 5511 248 5415))
